title: BindingObservation — one validator states what its own fetch derived
description: Signed by the VALIDATOR-INSTANCE key. It says: I fetched this post, I ran this method over what came back, and this is the binding I derived. It does NOT claim universal acceptance, and no field in it can. Acceptance is an application's decision under its own published policy.

captureHash.$comment: OPTIONAL signed provenance/audit metadata, and OUTSIDE ACCEPTANCE (R13R-B06, GPT-R4DR-B01, GPT-R4DR-R2-02). Absence is structurally admissible: an observation omitting it is fully conforming and is accepted on identical terms. When present it IS signed, because `sig` is the only member the artifact projection omits. It is not in the binding and not in bindingHash. Presence, absence, equality and inequality never affect acceptance or any validator-independence claim. V1 acceptance is bindingHash equality and nothing else. R13-A's fold required capture hashes to DIFFER, which added a second comparison law to the acceptance path and contradicted its own statement that honest validators merely SHOULD differ. A reader may compare capture hashes and draw conclusions; no acceptance outcome may depend on it. See EVIDENCE_FOLD.md section 4.

observedAt.$comment: the value this validator passed to the method. A CLAIM about its own clock, believable to nobody as objective time — MethodSpec section 11.2.

authorizationRef.$comment: the artifactId of the ValidatorAuthorization this key observes under

$comment: captureHash IS OPTIONAL (GPT-R4DR-B01). The R4 candidate carried it in `required`, which contradicts the controlling authoring order §4.9: it remains optional provenance and is never an acceptance or independence gate. A mandatory Stage-A member IS an acceptance gate whatever the prose beside it says. The property stays declared with its sha256 format; when present it is signed, because `sig` is the only member the artifact projection omits. Presence, absence, equality and inequality all stay outside acceptance.
